description.narrative: Insatsen bedöms bidra till målen för Resultatstrategin för Sidas strategi för Regionalt Asien och Oceanien 2022-2026. Den föreslagna garantin är en garanti för att täcka lån som ges ut under en obligation. Lånen ska användas till små-medelstora företag för att ge kvinnor tillgång till kapital, främja jämlikhet och Womens’s Ecnomic Empowerment, WEE. Insatsen bedöms vara i enlighet med förordning (2018:298) om garantier för utvecklingssamarbete och tillämpliga delar av förordning (2011:211) om utlåning och garantier. Den föreslagna garantin till IIX bedöms vara additionell då IIX inte skulle ha möjlighet att ge ut en obligation med storleken 60 MUSD utan Sidas deltagande.

The contribution aims to contribute to the goals for Sida's strategy for Regional Asia and Oceania 2022-2026. The purpose of the guarantee is to encourage greater committed capital volume in the bond, Women’s Livelihood Bond number 5 (WLB5) by reducing the risk for commercial and catalytic investors. WLB 5 is the fifth bond issued by IIX in their Women’s Livelihood Bond Series (WLB Series) and will be the first orange bond – a new asset class The proposed guarantee is a guarantee to cover loans issued under a bond. The loans are to be used for small and medium-sized companies to give women access to capital, promote equality and Women's Economic Empowerment, WEE. The proposed guarantee to IIX is deemed to be additional as IIX would not be able to issue a bond with the size of 60 MUSD without Sida's participation.

The objective of IIX support is (1) to build gender equality and support the economic empowerment of underserved women (defined as women from low-income, rural, minority, or otherwise economically disadvantaged families or communities) from the target countries (India, Indonesia, Cambodia, the Philippines) (2) empower women to create broader positive social and environmental impact including improving multigenerational impact (on dependent female beneficiaries), strengthening the women, peace and security agenda, and improving resilience to environmental shocks and stresses and (3) to advancing the broader gender lens investment movement and catalyze the sustainable finance ecosystem.

During 2025, the WLB5 portfolio-level impact performance remained within the expected range (/- 10% variance) for the number of women impacted and the Social Return on Investment (SROI: dollar value of social impact experienced by women impacted by WLB5 per dollar invested. It is a composite calculation of actual SROI from January 2024 to December 2025 and projected SROI till December 2027 (end of the bond tenor)):
Number of women directly impacted: 93 878, against an target range between 85,460 - 104,451 93,878
SROI: $3.69 against the target of $4
In terms of results from the proceeds connected to different SDG-targets, the following is noted:
~90,278 women from low-income communities were equipped to combat poverty through financial inclusion (SDG 1)
~17,737 women and girls experienced improved health outcomes including reduced risk of exposure to water-borne communicable diseases (SDG 2)
~3,176 women smallholder farmers were supported with agricultural loans to maintain and improve their yields, and combat growing pressures due to environmental changes (SDG 3)
~99,863 young women and girls benefited from financial support to stay longer in school (SDG4)
~93,878 women were empowered to sustain their livelihoods and better combat gender-based discrimination, advancing women empowerment through financial inclusion (SDG 5)
~10,587 women benefited from improved access to clean water and sanitation facilities, saving ~2 hours per day and improving their productivity (SDG 6)
~537 women and girls were provided access to clean and reliable energy sources (SDG 7)
~83,291 women were able to establish and maintain stable sources of income, including micro-entrepreneurs who were provided with affordable credit to sustain their businesses and women jobholders provided with decent employment (SDG 8)
US$50 million mobilized from developed countries towards emerging markets as official development assistance and foreign direct investment (SDG 10)
~3,637 women benefited from improved mobility and safety outcomes through access to electric vehicles and affordable housing loans, leading to improved security, shelter and sustainable transport outcomes (SDG 11)
~14,300 women empowered to build environmental resilience through access to clean energy (mitigation) and access to water or sustainable agricultural inputs (adaptation) (SDG 13)
WLB5 coalesced a range of public and private sector partners: 3 banks, 7 law firms, and 3 donor agencies (SDG 17)
Ahead of the Partner Meeting organized by the Embassy of Sweden in Bangkok on May 18-19 2026, IIX submitted a note summarizing some key impact results generated from the partnership with Sida. This partnership then includes all three guarantee contribution (to WLB5, WLB6 and WLB7). While kept on a very overarching level, it gives a flavor of what type of impact the guarantees are contributing to:
"Partnership with Sida: Institutional Change and Capacity Strengthening
Sidas partnership, alongside Global Affairs Canada, UNESCAP, and UNCDF, helped demonstrate that blended finance structures can mobilize institutional capital towards underserved women and enterprises in emerging markets. Through the WLB Series, Sidas support contributed to validating and scaling gender-lens investing across multiple bond issuances and geographies, while supporting the broader growth of the Orange Movement, which has mobilized over US$1.5 billion globally. At the borrower level, the WLB Series strengthened ESG and governance practices through impact covenants and the IIX Values framework, which assesses portfolio companies against IRIS, GRI, IFC Performance Standards and the UN SDGs. Several borrowers subsequently formalized environmental and sustainability policies, strengthened board-level ESG oversight, and introduced anti-bribery and labour monitoring mechanisms.
The partnership also strengthened transparency and accountability through semi-annual impact reporting, independent second-party verification, direct engagement with end borrowers through multilingual surveys and impact verification processes. All WLB issuances are independently assessed for compliance with both the Orange Bond Principles and ICMA Sustainability Bond Guidelines, strengthening credibility and consistency across the bond lifecycle. This reporting and verification infrastructure has contributed to stronger standards for impact measurement within gender-lens investing and blended finance markets."
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
